content.title: About
content.content: Lime juice 100% non‑sweetened (NS) is produced from fresh limes by cold pressing. The juice retains the natural aroma, bright acidity, and a rich vitamin profile characteristic of lime.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Lime provides over 30 mg of vitamin C per 100 ml, more than orange juice.
Traditionally used in Mexican, Thai and Vietnamese cuisines to add fresh tanginess.
Lime juice is often used in cosmetics as a skin‑toning rinse because of its antioxidant properties.
Lime is one of the few citrus fruits high in flavonoids such as naringenin.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system, collagen synthesis and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids and carotenoids in lime juice help neutralize free radicals.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: The acids in lime stimulate gastric juice production, improving food digestion.

items.title: May reduce kidney stone risk
items.content: Citric acid present in the juice can help dissolve small oxalate stones.

items.title: Supports weight control
items.content: Low‑calorie yet flavorful, lime juice can replace higher‑calorie sauces and dressings.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: High acidity may irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcers.

items.title: Citrus allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to lime juice.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Lime acids can enhance the effect of certain medications, such as anticoagulants.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Add lime juice to cocktails, marinades, sauces, salads and desserts. For drinks, dilute with water or use as a flavor boost in smoothies.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the juice in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C in a tightly sealed container. After opening, use within 5–7 days. Discard if the color, smell or taste changes.
